registry_disposition.reason: Scope is S2 wave 2 of the PROPOSED MAWS-SII-TARGET-SPEC-001: a read-only instruction reference-graph module (runtime/instructions/instruction-resolver.mjs), a stdout-only CLI, and tests, layered over the wave 1 inventory source set. Determination under the closed relevance taxonomy: no registered record changed — the slice creates no contract (no file under core/contracts/ touched), no canonical claim (no authority-matrix or canonical-files edit), no authority mapping, no dependency or lifecycle binding, and no supersession; it is proposal-scoped implementation of a not-yet-adopted specification. The reference graph is analysis input only: dangling references are recorded as observations for the S3 auditor and nothing is repaired, loaded, activated, or promoted. Registry relevance will be re-evaluated when the SII slices land adopted contracts (the S1 CONTRACT_RECORD obligation for skill-feedback.schema.json remains pending by design until its own registry write). The change registration for this change is published in the Registry repository (baum777/unitera-registry) as registry/MAWS_INSTRUCTION_REFERENCE_GRAPH_2026_10_20_001.yaml and merged as 15ef3f3315d927150e05b4349ef4d2e59c29a88a (pull request 220); it is a representation of the change, not an object mutation caused by it. The contract field registry_commit_sha stays null: registry-disposition.v1 invariant 4 forbids a non-null value unless the status is UPDATED, and invariant 2 requires UPDATED to carry a non-empty affected_records list, which this change does not have because no registry-relevant class changed. The published registration SHA is therefore carried as publication evidence only, and only after the publication succeeded.
